evidence: §3: "`tp epic add <json>` (`--stdin`, `--bulk <ndjson>`), `tp epic set <id> <field>=<value>`, `tp epic remove <id>` and `tp epic import <file>` are the only writers" (`set` takes an epic id, so it reaches epic fields only). §2: "`milestone` is required on every epic and names one of them". §4: `unknown-milestone` is an error, and §3 says "a write that would introduce an error exits 1 ... and writes nothing". §7: "Workflow E — interview the topic → `tp epic add --bulk` → `tp epic lint` → ...". Counterexample: with no `.tp/epics.json`, `tp epic add '{"id":"a","milestone":"A",...}'` has an after-state with no track holding `A`, so it exits 1. spec/backlog/epics.md names no milestones/gates/tag_checks writer either.
finding: No writer can create or change the file-level fields `milestones`, `gates` or `tag_checks`, so Workflow E cannot start on a fresh project: `tp epic add --bulk` is its first write, and every epic it adds fails `unknown-milestone` because no track exists yet. After the first epics land, adding a milestone, a gate or a tag check is possible only through `tp epic import --force` of a whole hand-built file, which the agent cannot write in place (write-deny hook) and which exits 2 under TP_UNATTENDED.
suggestion: Either name the writer for the file-level fields (e.g. `tp epic set --milestones/--gate/--tag-check`, or let `tp epic import` of a file with zero epics seed them and say Workflow E starts there), add that step to Workflow E, and add a §9 row for the first write on an absent file.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:77-78 "`tp epic add <json>` ..., `tp epic set <id> <field>=<value>`, `tp epic remove <id>` and `tp epic import <file>` are the only writers"; :82-83 "`tp epic import` refuses to replace a file that already holds epics unless `--force`"; :46-48 top-level `milestones`/`gates`/`tag_checks`; :100 `unknown-milestone` is an error; :24-25 the file is "written only by `tp epic` writers"; :170 Workflow E starts with `tp epic add --bulk`; :159 findings leave "as a graph write through §3".
finding: The writers cannot write the top-level fields §2 defines and §4 lints against. `tp epic set <id> <field>=<value>` addresses one epic; `add`/`remove` act on epics; so `milestones`, `gates` and `tag_checks` are writable only by `tp epic import`, which refuses a file that holds epics unless `--force`. Consequences: (a) on a fresh project the first `tp epic add` of Workflow E always fails `unknown-milestone`, since no writer but import can create a track; (b) adding a milestone, a gate member or a tag check for the next topic requires a whole-file `import --force`; (c) `tp epic remove --force` of a gate member or a `provided_by` epic is refused by `gate-unknown-member`/`unprovided-tag-check` with no writer able to fix the gate first; (d) a `phase-economist` finding located `gate:<m>` has no §3 write to leave the round through, contradicting §5's 'A recorded finding leaves the round as a graph write through §3 or as a disposition'.
suggestion: Decide a writer for the file-level fields (e.g. `tp epic set --milestones/--gate <m>/--tag-check <tag>` or a `tp epic set-file <field>=<json>`), or state that the file is seeded and reshaped only by import and make import's merge/--force policy part of Workflow E.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:9-10 "reusing the spec loop's record, convergence and cap rules unchanged"; :152-153 "`--status --check` exits 0 only when the slice is converged and every mechanical check passes"; skills/tp/SKILL.md:284 "`done`/`done_by` (the loop verdict — `converged`, or `cap` when the round cap ended the loop with every finding of the latest round dispositioned; `--check`, `--record`, `next_action`, `tp resume` and `tp import` all read it)"; SKILL.md:705 "The loop is **done** (`done_by: cap`) when every finding of the latest round carries a disposition".
finding: §5's `--status --check` drops the spec loop's cap-done verdict while the spec claims the loop's cap rules are reused unchanged. In `tp review`, a loop the cap ended with every latest finding dispositioned is done (`done_by: cap`) and `--check` reads that verdict; here `--check` exits 0 only when converged, and `--status` carries no `done`/`done_by`. A slice that reaches `review_max_rounds` with every finding dispositioned can therefore never pass `--check`, and Workflow E ('until `--status --check` exits 0 → the next topic') can only proceed by raising the cap, an operator decision. Two correct implementations disagree: one ports `done_by: cap`, the other implements the literal 'only when converged'.
suggestion: Say `--check` exits 0 when the slice is done (converged or `done_by: cap`) and mechanical checks pass, and add `done`/`done_by` to the `--status` field list; or state the divergence as a decision and say how Workflow E leaves a capped slice.

evidence: §9 row 17: "row 6's chain, round 1 recorded with no findings, one `why` edited before the first emission and nothing edited before the second". The header says the loop reuses "the spec loop's record, convergence and cap rules unchanged", and REFERENCE.md:642 says "Re-emitting an unrecorded round is idempotent while the spec is unchanged". §5: regression "is appended from round 2 when the slice changed since the round before".
finding: Row 17 contradicts the inherited re-emission rule unless round 2 is recorded between its two emissions, and the row does not say whether it is. If round 2 stays unrecorded, the second emission re-emits round 2 over the same slice. That is idempotent, so `regression` is appended again and the row's expectation ("over an unchanged slice it is not") fails. If round 2 is recorded clean first, the second emission is round 3, the slice is unchanged since round 2, and the expectation holds. Two correct implementations and two test authors will disagree.
suggestion: State in the fixture that round 2 is recorded with no findings before the second emission, so the second emission is round 3.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §2: "`milestones` is a list of tracks, each an ordered list of names. `milestone` is required on every epic and names one of them." §4 table has `unknown-milestone` (absent or in no track) but no rule for a name in more than one track; §6: "each epic's ... `track` added".
finding: Milestone names are not required to be unique across or within tracks, and no §4 rule catches a repeated name, yet an epic's track is derived from its milestone name alone. With `milestones: [["A","B"],["B"]]` an epic in `B` has two tracks, so `later-milestone-dependency` (same track or not), `no-dependencies` (first milestone of its track), export's `track` and `--md`'s one-table-per-milestone ordering each have two defensible answers.
suggestion: Decide that milestone names are unique across the whole file and add an error rule (e.g. `duplicate-milestone`), or say how a repeated name resolves.

evidence: §2: '`checks` entries have the workflow `checks` shape, `class` and `cmd`; this release stores and lints them and runs none.' §4's rule table has 10 rows and none of them concerns `checks` or `class`/`cmd`. §5's slice block lists 'id, title, milestone, tags, acceptance, each outgoing edge with its `why`, the gate it belongs to', with no checks.
finding: The `checks` arrays (on epics and in `tag_checks.<tag>.checks`) are described as 'stored and linted', but no rule in §4 reads them, the slice block in §5 does not render them, and nothing runs them. In this release they are schema, file bytes and export bytes that feed no agent decision, and two implementations would disagree on whether `checks` shape is validated. Only `tag_checks.<tag>.provided_by` feeds a rule (`unprovided-tag-check`).
suggestion: Remove `checks` from the epic and from `tag_checks.<tag>` in this release, keeping `tag_checks.<tag>.provided_by`. Bring them in with the second release, where status runs them. The backlog already defers `claimed_at`/`done` on the same grounds.

evidence: §2: "`id` is an opaque non-empty string, unique in the file". §4's table has ten rules and no duplicate-id rule. §3: writers run "§4's error rules over the file as it would be after the write". §9 row 2: "`tp epic add` would close a cycle | ... | a file with `a → b`; the payload sets `b → a`". Adding `b` again needs either a duplicate id or `tp epic set`.
finding: §2 says `id` is unique in the file, but no §4 rule enforces it, and §3's writers refuse only through §4's error rules. So `tp epic add` of an id that already exists could be refused, could upsert, or could append a duplicate, and `tp epic import` of a file with repeated ids passes every listed rule. Row 2 runs into this: it adds through `tp epic add` but "sets b → a" on an epic `b` the fixture already holds.
suggestion: Add a `duplicate-id` error rule (and an empty-id rule), and rewrite row 2's WHEN as `tp epic set b depends_on=...` or as an add of a new epic that closes the cycle.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §3: "runs §4's error rules over the file **as it would be after the write**: a write that would introduce an error exits 1 naming the rule and writes nothing." Row 2's mutant ("runs only the per-row rules") pins whole-file evaluation but not the baseline.
finding: "a write that would introduce an error" reads two ways when the file already holds an error (hand-edited, or produced by a future lint rule): (a) refuse whenever the post-write file has any error, which makes a file with two independent errors unrepairable one write at a time; or (b) refuse only errors absent before the write, which needs an identity for findings (a `cycle` finding's message changes as members change). Two correct implementations would accept and refuse different writes on the same file.
suggestion: State which: either the post-write file must be error-free, or a write is refused only for errors not present before it (and how findings are compared).

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:77 "`tp epic add <json>` (`--stdin`, `--bulk <ndjson>`), `tp epic set <id> <field>=<value>`, `tp epic remove <id>`"; :79-81 each write is checked "as it would be after the write" and "a write that would introduce an error exits 1"; :98 `dangling-dependency` is an error; CLAUDE.md P2 "What's easy for 1 task must be equally easy for N tasks".
finding: Only `add` has a batch form. `set` takes one field of one epic and `remove` one id, and each write is linted on its own. Repairing a review round's findings across N epics therefore takes N calls, which breaks P2, and a reshaping whose intermediate states are errors cannot be done at all. Renaming an epic id is the example: `set <id> id=<new>` dangles every inbound edge, so it is refused in any order, and the only route left is `remove --force` (which drops the inbound edges) plus re-adding them, or a whole-file `import --force`.
suggestion: Give `set`/`remove` a batch form applied atomically and linted once after the whole batch, so a multi-step reshape (including an id rename) is one write.

evidence: §3: "runs §4's error rules over the file **as it would be after the write**: a write that would introduce an error exits 1 naming the rule and writes nothing". The first clause supports A, "introduce" supports B. Row 11 already depends on a file that holds a lint error.
finding: The writers' error check can be read two ways. Reading A: refuse when the after-state holds any error. Reading B: refuse only when the write adds an error that was not there before. They differ on a file that already holds an error (hand-edited, or produced by a later release whose rule is new). Under A no write succeeds, including the repair of one of two errors. Under B an unrelated `tp epic add` succeeds. No row has a pre-existing error.
suggestion: Pick one (B is the only reading that allows incremental repair) and add a §9 row: a file holding a cycle, then an unrelated `tp epic add` and a `set` that breaks the cycle.

evidence: §4: each finding is "`{rule, severity, epic, message}` with `epic` null for a rule about the file as a whole", and `cycle` fires when "the dependency graph has a cycle; the message names its members". §9 row 3: "exit 1 with `errors` equal to the rule count and each error slug present exactly once", with fixture "a two-member cycle".
finding: How many findings a cycle produces is unspecified: one finding per cycle (with `epic` set to what?) or one per member. Row 3 asserts `errors` equals the rule count and that each slug appears exactly once, so a per-member implementation, which is equally correct by the table, fails row 3 with its two-member cycle.
suggestion: State that a cycle yields one finding per cycle and say what its `epic` field holds (null, or the lowest id).

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:60 "`id` is an opaque non-empty string, unique in the file"; :58-59 `milestone` "names one of them"; :79-81 writers run "§4's error rules over the file as it would be after the write"; :95-106 the rule table has no duplicate-id, duplicate-milestone or unknown-gate-key rule; :164 export adds `track`.
finding: §2 states invariants that no §4 rule enforces, so §3's write guard, which runs only §4's error rules, does not hold them. `id` is 'unique in the file', but there is no duplicate-id rule: `tp epic add` of an existing id and an import with duplicate ids pass lint, and two implementations will disagree on whether add appends or replaces. Milestone names have no uniqueness rule across tracks, which leaves an epic's track (and so `later-milestone-dependency` and export's `track`) undefined when a name appears in two tracks. A `gates` key naming no milestone also fires nothing.
suggestion: Add error rules (duplicate id, milestone name in two tracks, gate key naming no milestone), or narrow §2 to what §4 checks.

evidence: §5: "rendered one block per epic — id, title, milestone, tags, acceptance, each outgoing edge with its `why`, the gate it belongs to — with edges from outside the slice listed by id only". §5: "A finding on an edge belongs to the source epic's unit". §9 row 7: "exactly the edited epic un-carried in the second".
finding: "edges from outside the slice listed by id only" does not say which edges it means, because a block lists only outgoing edges. If it means a slice epic's outgoing edges into an epic outside the slice (c→d in the `--epic b` slice), the edge's `why` is omitted. Editing that `why` then leaves c's hash unchanged, so c stays `(carried)`, and `why-auditor` cannot judge the edge. If it means something else, c's block carries the `why` and the edit un-carries c. Row 7 edits "one why" without saying which, so its expectation splits on this reading.
suggestion: Say whether an outgoing edge to an out-of-slice epic keeps its `why` in the block (and so in the hash), and name the edited edge in row 7.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §5: "ejected by `tp init --eject-roles` and following the same file schema and activation rules"; §8.5: "No frontmatter overrides for graph roles."; skills/tp/SKILL.md:743 "`domain` selects the embedded corpus when no role files exist and filters a user corpus by each role's `domains`" (frontmatter `tp: domain:`); SKILL.md:745 `enabled` is a per-spec override.
finding: Graph roles follow "the same ... activation rules" as the reviewer and auditor corpora, but both of those rules take their input from spec frontmatter: `domain` filters the corpus by each role's `domains`, and per-spec `enabled: false` deactivates a role. A graph has no frontmatter, and §8.5 forbids frontmatter overrides for graph roles. The spec does not say what domain a graph has, whether `domains` on a graph role is honoured, or whether `tp init --eject-roles --domain prose` changes the graph corpus.
suggestion: State that every graph role is active (domains ignored, one default panel for every `--domain`), or name where a graph's domain comes from.

evidence: §2: "`id` is an opaque non-empty string ... spaces and non-ASCII included, stays as it is". §5: "Rounds are numbered per slice; the slice's state directory lives under `.tp-review/epics/`". §9 row 14: "`--milestone A` and `--epic b`".
finding: How a slice maps to its state directory is unspecified, and nothing stops two slice kinds from colliding. `--milestone A` and `--epic A`, with an epic whose id is `A`, could share one directory and one round count. Opaque ids may contain spaces, `/` or `..`, so an id used as a path component can escape `.tp-review/epics/`. Row 14 uses distinct names (`A` and `b`), so a mutant that keys the directory by the bare value passes it.
suggestion: Require the directory name to encode the slice kind and a safe form of the value (escaped or hashed), and give row 14 a milestone and an epic with the same name plus an id containing `/`.

evidence: §5: "§4's error rules run at every emission as `mechanical_checks`" and "`--status --check` exits 0 only when the slice is converged and every mechanical check passes". §5: "The slice is the named epics plus every epic one edge away", so for `--epic b` over a→b→c→d it is {a,b,c} (row 6). Row 11 fixture: "row 6's chain plus `d → a`", with no slice named.
finding: It is not stated whether `mechanical_checks` run §4's rules over the whole file or only over the slice. Row 11 depends on the answer. Its cycle a→b→c→d→a runs through `d`, and `d` is outside the `--epic b` slice that rows 6–10 use. A slice-scoped check sees no cycle and `--status --check` exits 0. A file-scoped check fails, but then any error anywhere in the graph (a dangling id in milestone L1, say) blocks every slice from converging.
suggestion: State the scope (whole file, or findings touching a slice epic), and name the slice in row 11's fixture.

evidence: §5: 'The slice is the named epics plus every epic one edge away in either direction.' / 'The unit is the epic block' / 'a unit whose hash is unchanged since the round before ... is not asked about again' / 'Rounds are numbered per slice'. §9 row 6: '--epic b ... the index lists a, b, c', so neighbours are units. §9 row 14: 'two state_dir values, both existing, neither inside the other', so carry state is not shared between slices. §7 Workflow E: '`tp epic review` over the touched slice until `--status --check` exits 0 → the next topic'.
finding: Neighbour epics are full review units in every slice they touch, but the carry and the round count are per slice, so an unchanged epic that has already converged in one slice is asked about again in round 1 of every other slice that contains it, and at least twice more before that slice converges. A milestone slice also pulls in every one-edge neighbour from other milestones as units. Workflow E reviews 'the touched slice' topic by topic, so the same epic keeps coming back across topics. That is the repeated question about an unchanged node that the loop was built to stop, moved from rounds to slices.
suggestion: Only the named epics are units. Render the one-edge neighbours as context (id, title, acceptance) that no prompt asks about and that `--record` does not accept as a `location`. This removes neighbour units, their hashes and their carry rows from every emission and leaves the role the context it needs.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:133 `dod-satisfiability` asks whether "none of its dependencies, transitively, provides"; :118-119 block = "id, title, milestone, tags, acceptance, each outgoing edge with its `why`, the gate it belongs to — with edges from outside the slice listed by id only"; :122-123 a unit "whose hash is unchanged since the round before and that carried no open finding is marked `(carried)`"; :159-160 "the next round re-asks exactly the units those writes changed".
finding: The carry key is narrower than what the `dod-satisfiability` role asks about. That role asks about each epic's transitive dependencies, but a unit is carried while its own block hash is unchanged, and the block holds only the epic's own fields and its outgoing edges. In chain a→b→c with slice `--epic b`, a `set` on c's acceptance that removes the capability b relies on changes only c's block: b is `(carried)` and is never re-asked, though its satisfiability answer changed. Beyond one hop the dependencies are not even rendered ('edges from outside the slice listed by id only'), so the role cannot answer 'transitively' from the emission at all.
suggestion: Either narrow the role to the dependencies the slice renders, or include the dependency closure's hashes (or the direct dependencies' acceptance) in a unit's carry key, and say which.

evidence: §5: "a unit whose hash is unchanged since the round before and that carried no open finding is marked `(carried)` ... unlike `tp ground`, a unit with an open finding is re-asked", against §5: "the next round re-asks exactly the units those writes changed". §9 row 7 fixture: "round 1 recorded with no findings". Row 17 is the same.
finding: The rule that separates this loop from `tp ground`, "a unit with an open finding is re-asked", has no §9 row: rows 7 and 17 both start from a round 1 with no findings, so a mutant that carries every unchanged unit regardless of open findings passes the whole table. §5's closing sentence also contradicts the rule for an unchanged unit that still has an open finding: "the next round re-asks exactly the units those writes changed".
suggestion: Add a row: round 1 records an open finding on `a` with no write; round 2 un-carries exactly `a`. Narrow the closing sentence to "changed units and units with an open finding".

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:151-152 `--status` carries `slice, round, consecutive_clean, converged, carried, in_flight_round, next_action` (no `stale`); :117 slice = named epics plus one edge away; :171 Workflow E moves to "the next topic" once `--check` exits 0; spec/backlog/epics.md:135-136 "An epic added mid-work with `discovered_from` reopens its neighbourhood's slice for one round"; skills/tp/SKILL.md:284 lists `stale` among review `--status` fields.
finding: The spec does not say what happens to a converged slice when the graph changes under it. Slices overlap (`--milestone A` and `--epic b` share epics, row 14) and Workflow E grows the graph topic by topic, so a later topic's `add` or another slice's repair edits epics in an already-converged slice, or changes its membership by adding an edge one hop away. `tp review` has `stale` (the spec changed since the last round) and it blocks done; §5's `--status` list has no `stale` and no slice hash. One implementation keeps the old slice `converged` forever. Another re-derives the slice, finds new or changed units and reopens it, which the backlog note intended ('An epic added mid-work with `discovered_from` reopens its neighbourhood's slice for one round').
suggestion: Decide whether a slice goes stale when its re-derived membership or any unit hash differs from the last recorded round, and whether stale blocks `--check`, as `tp review`'s staleness does.

evidence: §5: '§4's error rules run at every emission as `mechanical_checks`' and '`--status --check` exits 0 only when the slice is converged and every mechanical check passes.' §4 defines lint over 'the file'. §9 row 11 says 'the slice holds a cycle' and does not cover a cycle outside the slice.
finding: The spec does not say whether `mechanical_checks` at emission lint the slice or the whole file. Read as whole-file, an error in an unrelated milestone (from a merge or an edit outside the fence) makes `--status --check` exit 1 for every slice, and an agent reviewing milestone A spends rounds it cannot finish until it repairs epics outside its slice. Read as slice-only, that does not happen. The two correct implementations give different exit codes.
suggestion: State that `mechanical_checks` report only findings whose `epic` is in the slice (plus file-level rules), or state that they cover the whole file. Then remove the one row of §9 that the chosen reading makes untestable, rather than adding rows.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §5: "the slice's state directory lives under `.tp-review/epics/` and `--status` names it as `state_dir`"; skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:630 "tp owns the review/audit round lifecycle in `<spec-dir>/.tp-review/<spec-base>/`"; scripts/check-suite-state.sh:32 `WATCHED=(spec/.tp-review .tp/rounds)`.
finding: The state directory "lives under `.tp-review/epics/`" with no anchor. tp's existing rule derives `<spec-dir>/.tp-review/<spec-base>/` from the spec's own path, and a graph has no spec; candidates are the repo root, the `.tp/` directory beside `epics.json`, or a spec directory. The choice also decides whether the gate's suite-state check sees test pollution: it watches only `spec/.tp-review` and `.tp/rounds`.
suggestion: Name the parent directory (e.g. `.tp/` at the `.git` boundary, the same discovery as `epics.json`) and whether the suite-state check watches it.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:148 "`gate:<m>` for the slice's milestone"; :115 the slice is `--milestone <m>` or `--epic <id>`; :121 "The unit is the epic block"; :124-125 only edge findings are mapped to a unit; spec/backlog/epics.md:107 "a finding on a gate to the milestone's" (not carried into 1.3.0).
finding: `gate:<m>` findings have no unit and no defined slice milestone. A `gate:<m>` row is valid only 'for the slice's milestone', which exists for `--milestone` but not for an `--epic` slice, whose epics may span milestones and tracks. One implementation refuses every gate row on an `--epic` slice; another accepts the named epic's milestone, or any milestone in the slice. Units are epic blocks, and the backlog's rule that a gate finding belongs to the milestone's unit was dropped. So the carry rule ('carried no open finding') and the `phase-economist` gate question have no unit to attach to: an open gate finding neither prevents nor forces any re-ask.
suggestion: Define the slice's milestone(s) for `--epic` (or forbid `gate:` there), and say which unit or units a gate finding belongs to for the carry.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §5: "§4's error rules run at every emission as `mechanical_checks`"; "`--status --check` exits 0 only when the slice is converged and every mechanical check passes"; §9 row 11: "the slice holds a cycle".
finding: §4's error rules run "at every emission as `mechanical_checks`", and `--status --check` exits 0 only when "every mechanical check passes", but the spec does not say whether the checks are scoped to the slice or run over the whole file. A cycle among epics outside the slice either blocks this slice's convergence (whole-file) or not (slice-scoped); and slice-scoping is itself unclear for rules that need the whole graph (`unprovided-tag-check` walks the transitive closure beyond one edge). Row 11 only covers a cycle inside the slice.
suggestion: Say whether a slice's mechanical checks are the whole file's lint or only the findings whose `epic` is in the slice (and what happens to file-level findings with `epic` null).

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:204 row 7 "round 2 is emitted over an unchanged slice, then over one edited `why`"; :214 row 17 "one `why` edited before the first emission and nothing edited before the second" expecting no `regression` the second time; :137-138 regression appended "when the slice changed since the round before"; skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:642 "if the spec changed since the emission, `tp ground`, `tp review` and `tp audit` exit 3 naming the round".
finding: Rows 7 and 17 do not say whether their second emission is round 2 re-emitted or round 3 after recording round 2, and under the reused rules the readings give different results. Row 17: if the second emission re-emits in-flight round 2, the slice still differs from round 1, so §5's rule appends `regression`, the opposite of the row's expectation. Row 7: re-emitting an unrecorded round after its source changed exits 3 without `--force` in the spec loop, so 'then over one edited why' fails unless round 2 was recorded in between, and then the comparison is against round 2, not round 1.
suggestion: State in each fixture which rounds are recorded between the two emissions (e.g. 'round 2 recorded clean, then round 3 emitted').

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §4 rows `gate-unknown-member` ("a gate's member or deferrable names no epic") and `unprovided-tag-check` ("`provided_by` is not in its transitive dependencies"); no row covers the gate key or `provided_by` itself.
finding: Two references in the file have no rule: a `gates` key that names no milestone (then `gate-member-outside-milestone` compares against a milestone that does not exist), and a `tag_checks.<tag>.provided_by` that names no epic (then `unprovided-tag-check` fires on every carrier with a message that blames the dependency closure rather than the dangling provider). Implementations will differ on whether these fire, and under which slug.
suggestion: Either extend `gate-unknown-member`/`dangling-dependency` to the gate key and `provided_by`, or state that those cases fire under an existing slug.

evidence: §4: `missing-why` fires on "an edge [with] no `why`, or one that is empty once trimmed", and `thin-why` on "a `why` [that] equals, or is wholly contained in, the target epic's id or title".
finding: `thin-why` ("wholly contained in" the target's id or title) also fires on an empty `why`, because the empty string is contained in every string. Every `missing-why` edge therefore also gets a `thin-why` warning. One implementation reports both, another skips empty values, and the `warnings` counts differ.
suggestion: Say that `thin-why` applies only to a non-empty trimmed `why`.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md:104 "an epic carries a tag whose `tag_checks.provided_by` is not in its transitive dependencies"; :48 `"ui": {"provided_by": "ui-rule-checker"}`.
finding: `unprovided-tag-check` fires on the provider epic itself whenever it carries the tag it provides, because an epic is not in its own transitive dependencies. A `ui-rule-checker` tagged `ui` can never land through the writers. The spec does not say whether the provider is exempt.
suggestion: Exempt the `provided_by` epic from its own tag's rule, or say the provider must not carry the tag.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §5: "The slice is the named epics plus every epic one edge away in either direction. The whole graph is never emitted." §9 row 14 fixture: "`--milestone A` and `--epic b` over row 6's chain in milestone `A`".
finding: "The whole graph is never emitted" contradicts row 14's fixture, where `--milestone A` over a four-epic chain all in milestone `A` emits the whole graph. An implementer who reads the sentence as a guard (refuse a slice equal to the graph) fails row 14; if it only means there is no whole-graph mode, the sentence restates "exactly one of the two" and can go.
suggestion: Delete the sentence, or reword it as "there is no whole-graph mode".

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §5: "a unit whose hash is unchanged since the round before and that carried no open finding is marked `(carried)` ... a unit with an open finding is re-asked" vs "the next round re-asks exactly the units those writes changed."
finding: "the next round re-asks exactly the units those writes changed" conflicts with the carry rule two paragraphs up. A unit with an open finding is re-asked though unchanged, and a write that adds an edge brings a never-asked neighbour into the slice that no write changed, and it must be asked because it has no prior hash. Read literally, "exactly" would carry both.
suggestion: Drop "exactly", or restate the closing sentence in terms of the carry rule (re-asked = changed, new to the slice, or holding an open finding).

evidence: §6: '`--json` writes the file's content with each epic's `in_degree`, `out_degree` and `track` added; ... `--compact` applies to both.' §8.3: 'No rendering. No ASCII, mermaid or HTML map.' No other section reads these three fields.
finding: `tp epic export --json` adds `in_degree`, `out_degree` and `track` to every epic. No command, role or workflow step in this release reads them: `track` is a lookup of `milestone` in `milestones`, and the degrees are counts of data in the same payload. Their stated consumer is a renderer, which §8.3 excludes. '`--compact` applies to both' names no field that `--compact` would strip from the `--md` table, so the flag has no defined effect there.
suggestion: Export the file's content unchanged in this release and drop the three derived fields until a reader exists. Limit the `--compact` sentence to `--json`, or drop it.

evidence: §3: "Under `TP_UNATTENDED` every writer exits 2 and writes nothing". §9 row 12: "`tp epic add` and `tp epic review --record` exit 2". Row 16 covers import. No row runs set or remove under TP_UNATTENDED.
finding: Row 12 fences `tp epic add` and `--record` only (row 16 adds `import`). A mutant that leaves `tp epic set` and `tp epic remove` unfenced under TP_UNATTENDED passes every row, although §3 fences every writer.
suggestion: Extend row 12 to all four writers.

evidence: spec/1.3.0.md §9 row 17 fixture: "round 1 recorded with no findings, one `why` edited before the first emission and nothing edited before the second"; §5: "`regression` role is appended from round 2 when the slice changed since the round before"; row 7 uses two emissions of round 2.
finding: Row 17's second emission has no stated round, and the regression rule compares against "the round before". If it re-emits round 2 without recording (as row 7 does with its two emissions), the slice is still changed relative to round 1 and `regression` must be appended, which contradicts the row's "over an unchanged slice it is not". If it is round 3, the fixture must record round 2, and it does not say so.
suggestion: Make row 17's fixture record round 2 (no findings) between the two emissions, so the second emission is round 3.
